script: You can't even pee alone. Here's the real reason your dog follows you into the bathroom every single time. Dogs descended from pack animals, and for a pack, staying together wasn't just social, it was survival. Splitting up meant more vulnerability, so your dog's brain is still wired with a strong instinct to keep the group together, and in a modern household, you are the group. This kind of behavior even has a nickname, velcro dog, and it tends to show up more in breeds bred specifically to work alongside humans rather than off on their own. Every time your dog checks in on you, even through a closed door, their brain gets a small hit of oxytocin, the same bonding chemical released during affection and eye contact. For most dogs, this is simply loyalty and comfort, nothing to worry about. But if the following becomes frantic, or turns into visible panic the moment you're out of sight, that shift from companionship to distress can be an early sign of separation anxiety, and that's worth addressing with structured training. For the vast majority of dogs though, that bathroom door incident is just your best friend making sure the pack stays together.
